svg.title: Deal Percentages on Assigned and Purchased Judgments
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-assignment-deal-percentages; chapter number: 2; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Deal Percentages on Assigned and Purchased Judgments; subtitle: Splits, payback shares, fees, and garnishment ceilings quoted by practitioners; unit: percent; caption: Operators keep one-third to one-half of collections, Lance runs a straight 50/50 split, Schmidt pays original creditors 15 to 20 percent on future-pay buys, and wage garnishment tops out at 25 percent of gross pay per Greg.; assumptions note: Where a practitioner gave a range, typical is either the figure they called standard or the arithmetic midpoint (17.5 for Schmidt's 15 to 20 percent). Single-figure claims show the same min, max, and typical.; note: Sources - Cross the River, Find the Treasure (TiGcICs90xE), Judgment Recovery Training Online with Lance (L2dopNFjS6s), cynthia schmidt (t_Wf5tSZn4s), InfoUSA1 with Greg of Ford Judgment Recovery (OjrZdehs8Xk), LeanLaw (pmUaXhIL3eA).; bars: label: Operator Share of Collections; min: 33.33; max: 50; typical: 50; display: One-third to one-half, 50 percent standard on small claims; label: Lance Contingency Split; min: 50; max: 50; typical: 50; display: 50/50 with no fees to the creditor; label: Contingency Fee in Settlement Demo; min: 33.33; max: 33.33; typical: 33.33; display: 33.33 percent on a $10,000 settlement; label: Wage Garnishment Ceiling; min: 25; max: 25; typical: 25; display: Up to 25 percent of gross pay per paycheck; label: Future-Pay Share to Original Creditor; min: 15; max: 20; typical: 17.5; display: 15 to 20 percent until satisfied
